pages.Field Note — Day 3: Whoever wrote this woke to a lantern they didn't light. So did I.
pages.from the pack: One more print going in than coming out. Something stayed in this house. Maybe that's me.
pages.torn page: Bare branches in a shape. I've been telling myself the tree line is only branches, too.
pages.the handwriting changes: If the hand that waved is the hand that wrote this, whose hand came back to the cabin?
pages.don't: Stay. Finish. Don't go to the lights. Everything on this page wants me standing still.
pages.by the bed: They burned the candle down so they'd know if they'd been here before. It's burned down, and I don't remember.
pages.intake: The strap said M. Whoever copied it wrote R. Either they read it wrong, or it changed for them.

places.bedroom: The blanket's warm on the side I didn't sleep on.
places.hall: One way out, and the mat's lying perfectly straight, like nobody ever came in.
places.living: Somebody sat up with that candle until it went out. Keeping watch, or waiting to be let in.
places.backhall: Any other house would have a back door. This one only goes down.
places.stair: Count the steps. If there's one more on the way back up, I'm done counting.
places.landing: Down here the wind's gone. If anything else is breathing, I'll hear it.
places.corridor: No windows. Whatever this house keeps, it keeps down here.
places.janitor: Someone mopped this floor. Someone cleans up after whatever happens here.
places.morgue: A drawer for every one of us. I'm not going to count them.
places.snow: My own prints are the only thing out here I can trust. So I'll keep counting them.
places.lights: They've been on since before the snow. Nobody leaves an engine running that long for a stranger.

bored: Standing still is exactly how the pages wanted me. I should move.
Mara. I keep saying it, to hear if it sounds like mine.
I keep watching my right hand, as if it might wave without me.
Three knocks, the page said. I've been waiting for the first one.
If I stop counting my breaths, is anything else keeping count?
Nobody is out here looking for me. Or nobody knows who to look for.
Somewhere, someone wrote down how tall I am. I'd rather they'd written my name.
The road is closed, the lights are on, and I'm the only one still walking toward them.
